claims.claim: Identity/tradability are validated for Monolithic Power Systems (NASDAQ:MPWR; CIK 0001280452).
Direct SEC Q2 filing and 2026 proxy provide primary financial/governance lineage; current independent market valuation is separated from issuer evidence.

risks.risk: High valuation, Enterprise Data concentration, outsourced manufacturing dependence and the 2026 restatement raise the execution/confidence bar.

unknowns.unknown: Foundry-partnership production volume, economics and timing remain undisclosed.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue reached $980.6M, up 47.6% year over year, with Enterprise Data $380.6M and Q3 revenue guidance of $1.14B-$1.16B.
MPS is fabless and relies on third parties to manufacture, assemble and test ICs; the September GlobalFoundries partnership is a resilience action but not yet proven production economics.
At September 22 close MPWR was about $1,380.62 with $67.85B market cap and roughly 84x trailing earnings, making valuation demanding despite growth.

risks.risk: 84x trailing valuation, AI/server concentration, third-party manufacturing, socket substitution and prior-period restatement can compress returns if execution slips.

unknowns.unknown: Detailed economics and ramp schedule of the new foundry partnership are not established.

thesisQuality.basis: Exceptional current adoption and revenue growth in power management support durable demand, tempered by concentration and substitution risk.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: 47.6% YoY Q2 growth and materially higher Q3 guide show exceptional operating acceleration.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: About 84x trailing earnings and $67.85B market cap require aggressive outcomes despite strong growth.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 growth guide and manufacturing partnership are identifiable near-term catalysts with source support.

governancePower.basis: Current proxy supports established governance and incentive structures, while the 2026 restatement prevents a stronger transparency score.

alignment2036.basis: Efficient power conversion is foundational across AI compute, communications, automotive and industrial electrification.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Core power-management capability serves Enterprise Data, storage/computing, automotive, industrial and communications markets.

bottleneckControl.basis: Power conversion is a critical constraint in high-density compute, but MPS does not exclusively control the layer.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Multiple end markets diversify demand, offset by rising Enterprise Data concentration.

substitutionResilience.basis: Design/qualification barriers support resilience, but architecture shifts and competing socket wins remain credible.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Diversification actions are positive, but fabless third-party manufacturing remains a material dependency and partnership ramp is unproven.

pricingPower.basis: Rapid growth and specialized power content imply strong value capture, though current evidence does not prove structurally protected pricing across cycles.

riskEvidence.basis: Demand concentration, high valuation, outsourced supply, substitution risk and restatement history create above-moderate risk.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Direct SEC financial and governance filings plus current market evidence cover all score dimensions; foundry economics and customer-level concentration remain incomplete.

scoreRecord.thesis: MPS has exceptional AI/electrification power-management momentum and cross-market leverage, but valuation and execution expectations are unusually demanding.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: AI/server concentration or architecture/socket loss collides with an 84x trailing valuation and outsourced supply dependence.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 earnings against the $1.14B-$1.16B revenue guide and evidence of GlobalFoundries ramp conversion.
